article.headline: Scotland thumped by Switzerland in Nations League, pressure grows on Sebastien Pocognoli
article.description: Andy Robertson became Scotland's most capped male player as Sebastien Pocognoli came under pressure with a bruising 4-0 Nations League defeat in Switzerland.
article.linkText: Scotland thumped by Switzerland in Nations League
article.story:
Andy Robertson became Scotland's most capped male player but his side were thumped 4-0 by Switzerland in the Nations League, a result which puts more pressure on coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

The 32-year-old Tottenham left-back overtook previous record holder Sir Kenny Dalglish by making his 103rd appearance in the Berit Sitterstadion, but it was a night to forget for the Tartan Army who left St Gallen beleaguered.

The Scots were comfortable against the much-changed Group B1 winners until the 22nd minute when midfielder Lewis Ferguson put through his own goal.

The unforced error deflated the visitors, who lost wing-back Aaron Hickey to injury before the break, and there was more damage in the 47th minute when Samuel Ballet's drive was touched in by Winsley Boteli before Alvyn Sanches hammered in a third just four minutes later, with substitute Zeki Amdouni adding a late fourth.

The Scots finished third in the group behind Switzerland and Slovenia, with seven points from 18, missing out on a promotion play-off spot next year and a more favourable seeding for the 2028 European Championship qualifying draw next month.

The Belgian boss' first campaign as Steve Clarke's successor has been underwhelming to say the least with just two wins -- both against bottom side North Macedonia -- from six fixtures and Pocognoli now finds himself under the spotlight just months into his tenure.
